clue.text: 'Now you might feel the pinch' (T May?)

parts.note: T is the first letter of the word 'the', and May is an example of a month, so the two clue words are what that phrase would build

explanation.surface: A wry aside about Theresa May, the former prime minister, feeling the pinch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T May' looks like the politician Theresa May, but read it as wordplay: T is the first of 'the' and May is a month. The definition quotes a British children's custom of saying 'a pinch and a punch' on the first day of a new month.
explanation.definitionFit: British children greet the start of each calendar period with 'a pinch and a punch', so that day is when one feels the pinch.

clue.text: Right-hand man who always produces the circular letter

definitions.meaning: a deputy, the person ranking just below the leader

definitions.text: who always produces the circular letter
definitions.meaning: the letter in second place of the word 'command' is O, the round letter, so this phrase always yields that circle

explanation.surface: A trusted deputy who forever churns out the same circular to the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular letter' looks like a memo sent round an office; it is the letter O, which always sits second in the word 'command'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy or chief lieutenant is the officer ranking directly beneath the leader, a person's right-hand man.

clue.text: Fish supper without superior beer is rubbish

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: without means the letters of the following word are taken away from supper

parts.note: superior means upper, as in the upper class
wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: Complaining that a fish supper served with no decent beer is a poor show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes UPPER from SUPPER, leaving just S. WALLOP is old British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang word for nonsense, talk or ideas that are worthless drivel.

clue.text: Fellow keeping the Queen up after midnight? That's highly unlikely!

indicators.note: keeping means the fellow holds the other pieces within him

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters for the Queen are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina
a.m. means ante meridiem, the hours after midnight

explanation.surface: A university man keeping the monarch up past midnight, and a scoffing reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after midnight' looks like timing for the surface, but it stands for the morning hours abbreviation; in a down clue 'up' turns the Queen's cipher back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic retort telling someone their hopes are fantasy and will never come true.

clue.text: Pacific island where American has to stick around

indicators.note: around means the sticking word goes round the abbreviation for American

parts.note: to gum something is to stick it down

explanation.surface: An American visitor forced to hang about on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts A inside GUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A US territory in the western Pacific, the largest of the Mariana Islands.

clue.text: V-day?

parts.note: V is the letter in third place of the eleventh month's name, so a 'V day' is that date in the calendar

explanation.walkthrough: V-day looks like VE Day or Valentine's Day, or the fifth of a month by Roman numerals; instead V is the third letter of NOVEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter V sits third in the name of the eleventh month, so the clue's day is that calendar date.

clue.text: Time of month one is under strain

indicators.note: to strain is to distort or force out of shape, so these letters are pulled into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a time in the month when someone is under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like part of 'under strain' but is the anagram signal: OF MONTH, I and IS UNDER are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, time is treated as an extra dimension added to the three spatial ones of length, breadth and height.

clue.text: Got rid of jumper after a flipping emergency exit

indicators.note: after means the jumper's letters come behind the firing word

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them, getting rid of them

indicators.note: flipping means the word for the jumper is turned back to front

parts.note: roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumping animal

explanation.surface: Someone sacked a kangaroo, then a cursed escape route appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads like a mild British expletive before 'emergency exit', but it turns the jumper round; 'a' is only padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-resistant door used to escape a building in an emergency or slow the spread of flames.

clue.text: Release a foreign film featuring Peter Pan

parts.note: un is the French word for a
Hook is a 1991 Spielberg film with Robin Williams as a grown-up Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A distributor releasing a foreign-language film about Peter Pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' looks like a film release, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something by undoing the catch or fastening that holds it, as with a dress or a fish.

clue.text: One northerner's neckwear

parts.note: a means one, as in a single item
a Scot is someone from the north of Britain; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Describes a Scotsman's cravat or scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad neckties or cravats, named after the racecourse where they were fashionable, are worn around the throat.

clue.text: Those who very much like being married, sadly single

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of married are disordered

explanation.surface: People who love being wed, regretfully single now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MARRIED; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans or devotees are people who hold someone or something in high regard.

clue.text: Cross over, right through openings of 7

indicators.note: through means the short pieces pass into the middle of the openings

parts.note: the first letters of the two words of the answer to 7 down, Fourth and Dimension
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Reads as crossing over with a right turn through some openings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' puts O and R between F and D, the first letters of FOURTH DIMENSION (7 down).
explanation.definitionFit: To wade across a river or stream at a shallow place; the verb also names that crossing place.

clue.text: If letters were missing, this could be the fourth character of eight in a string

definitions.text: If letters were missing, this could be the fourth character of eight in a string

indicators.note: if the letters went missing the answer would be what remains, so they are put back into what remains
in means the picked character goes inside the string

parts.note: a rope is a string or cord

indicators.note: the fourth character of the word eight is picked out

parts.note: post is mail, letters delivered

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which character sits fourth in a string of text.
explanation.walkthrough: Take POST (letters) out of the answer and AROPHE remains: H, the fourth letter of EIGHT, placed in A ROPE (a string). The whole clue also defines it, since this mark shows letters are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark stands where letters are left out, as in don't or o'clock.

clue.text: Thrower of tantrums, perhaps one that's ridden in 10 Queen Mary Stakes

definitions.meaning: a toddler in the 'terrible twos', a stage known for tantrums

definitions.text: one that's ridden in 10 Queen Mary Stakes
definitions.meaning: the Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot (10 across) is a race for young fillies in their second year

explanation.walkthrough: '10' points to ASCOTS; the Queen Mary Stakes is run at Royal Ascot, a famous English racecourse, for juvenile horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a young child given to tantrums and a juvenile racehorse are described by age.

clue.text: Quivering with delight due to funny tag line

indicators.note: funny means odd or strange, so the letters of tag line are put into a peculiar order

explanation.surface: Thrilled by a comic slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling a thrill or prickle of excitement, a tingling sensation of pleasure.

clue.text: House number in guarantee, a provider of sole security

indicators.note: in means the number goes inside the guarantee

parts.note: bail is money given as a guarantee that a defendant will appear

explanation.surface: An insurance policy for a house, giving financial security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the only one, but it means the sole of a boot, which this big-headed nail grips.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy-headed nail hammered into boot soles to make them hard-wearing and give grip.

clue.text: Implant essential: need good root alternative for tooth, initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of each word from essential to tooth are taken

explanation.surface: Dental advice: an implant is essential when a tooth needs a good root substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: To graft or insert tissue into the body, as a surgeon implants a substitute.

clue.text: Republican 19 reportedly receives green money as payment

indicators.note: receives means the green money goes into the Republican's name
reportedly means we hear the vice-president's surname spoken

parts.note: the answer at 19 is a vice-president, and Mike Pence was the Republican one at the time
eco is a prefix for environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: A vice-president rumoured to take environmental cash as a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is the vice-president, Mike Pence under Trump; 'reportedly' is needed because the answer spells his name's sound with S, not C.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation or reward given for loss, trouble or service, a kind of remuneration.

clue.text: 5p's about equivalent to what 12 was once

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: about means the letter's name is turned round

parts.note: pee is how the letter P is spelt out

explanation.surface: Seems to compare a five-pence coin with an old value.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is FORD: Gerald Ford was vice-president before he became president; 'equivalent to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial American nickname for the vice-president, which Gerald Ford was under Nixon.

clue.text: More usual term for an MP?

definitions.meaning: an elected member sits in the House of Commons, so may be called a member of the lower house

explanation.walkthrough: An MP is a Member of Parliament in the British House of Commons, the lower house.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of ordinary, and also a non-noble person or member of the Commons.

clue.text: 10 veg in one pie, cooked before 10 leaves

definitions.note: 10 across points to the Scots, so a Scottish vegetable

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of one pie are mixed up
leaves means the letters of ten depart from the mix

parts.note: ten in digits is a one and a zero, read as I and O

explanation.surface: A Scottish vegetable baked in a pie, cooked before the Scots leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix ONE PIE and remove IO (10 as figures) to leave the letters. The same '10' in the definition means Scots. A Scottish word for turnip or swede, eaten with haggis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish dialect name for a turnip or swede, served as 'tatties and' with haggis.

clue.text: Careless Whisper, heartily covered by Island rock band first

indicators.note: first means the band comes at the front

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band

indicators.note: covered by means the heart letter sits inside the island abbreviation
heartily means the central letter of whisper is taken

explanation.surface: Evokes George Michael's song Careless Whisper, with a rock band going first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careless Whisper' looks like the song title, but 'Careless' alone is the definition. 'heartily' takes S from WHISPER and 'covered by' puts it inside IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent or lax in duty; being remiss means failing to take proper care.

clue.text: Attitude shown by earliest ancestors

indicators.note: shown by means the letters are on display within earliest ancestors

explanation.surface: An outlook displayed by our first forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A position or point of view on an issue, a person's attitude or standpoint.

clue.text: Dessert containing large foreign article is a showy but worthless trifle

indicators.note: containing means the dessert holds the other pieces

parts.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit purée and cream
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: A pudding holding a big foreign item, and a sneer about a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the British pudding, alongside 'Dessert', but it means a trinket. A fool is a British fruit-and-cream pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaudy but valueless trinket or ornament, or nonsense; a fal-de-lal.
